note: Code derivation: the IRW item IS the source column name (data/ders16_xiong_2025.R pivots starts_with('lec') and renames nothing), but the .sav files carry NO variable labels and NO value labels on lec1..lec17 (checked in all four files), and the codebook names the instrument only. So the tie lecN -> LEC-5 event N is an inference that the study numbered its columns in the instrument's order: mapping_basis=paper_order (order of the canonical form, not of this study's paper, which was not accessible). Step 5b route 8 with a between-sample contrast, PARTIAL -- see verify_lec5_xiong_2025.R. Text: all 17 item_text strings are verbatim substrings of the NCPTSD LEC-5 Standard PDF (17/17 checked mechanically after whitespace collapse); DEVIATION: leading item numbers stripped. resp: 0/1 is the study's own exposure indicator, not a response option any respondent saw -- the .sav LEC_T equals the row sum of lec1..lec17 in the college, community and prisoner files (100% of rows). The binarisation rule is not stated in the deposit; the same group's open-access LEC-5 papers (Geng et al. 2021 EJPT PMC8075087; Zhan et al. 2021 PMC8276668) administer the six-category form and count the first four categories (happened to me / witnessed it / learned about it / part of my job) as exposure, which is probably what 1 means here but is NOT confirmed for this study. Hence option_text blank (no label exists to transcribe) and instructions blank (the official instructions describe the six-category format; whether this study administered that format is undocumented in the deposit) -- same shape as orovou_2021_lec5. LANGUAGE: four Chinese samples; the administered Chinese LEC-5 wording is in neither the deposit (.sav files: no labels; codebook: English, 6 lines) nor any accessible supplement, so the Step-4 fallback applies: canonical English in the base fields, language=Chinese, _translated columns omitted (orovou_2021_lec5 precedent). RIGHTS: register row 'Life Events Checklist for DSM-5 (LEC-5)' verdict ship_with_note applied, not re-derived. The measure page's one caution, quoted: 'These measures are intended for use by qualified mental health professionals and researchers.' (https://www.ptsd.va.gov/professional/assessment/te-measures/life_events_checklist.asp, register sha256 025148331b3d9e1fa1d6bf7f2a85f3a3b82c7ebac56ed6e8afaf0e434082e169). It describes intended users and reserves no right (fee, permission, NC, ND or redistribution), so under the 2026-09-08 LOT-R rule it does not block. Data note (not a defect claim): Adolescent_data.sav fails to parse under UTF-8/GBK/GB18030 and reads lec3..lec17 as empty under latin1; the processing script used Adolescent_data.csv instead and the live table has n=9506 on every item, so this affects only re-reading the .sav, not the IRW table.
public_note: The item wording is the English LEC-5 Standard form from the US National Center for PTSD, not the Chinese version these four samples completed (which the study did not publish), and resp is the study's own 0/1 exposure indicator (1 = exposed to the event) rather than one of the LEC-5's six response categories; the rule used to collapse those categories is not documented in the data deposit.

But the deposit carries no item wording at all: pcl1..pcl20 have no SPSS variable labels and no value labels in any of the four .sav files; the only labels in the files are sex, the cluster-score columns R/A/NACM/H and the *_YN flags; codebook_ders-16.txt says only 'PCL = Posttraumatic Stress Disorder Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5)'. The Mplus folders hold outputs and .dat files only. So MAPPING (paper_order): pclN is taken to be PCL-5 standard-form item N from the code's numeric suffix, i.e. canonical presentation order; checked in Step 5b (PARTIAL: cluster membership of all 20 items pinned by the deposit's own R/A/NACM/H scores; pcl16 pinned as marker; within-cluster order not pinned). TEXT (translated_substitute, official_instrument_english): administered in Chinese (four Chinese samples: adolescents, college students, community adults, male prisoners), but no Chinese wording is in the deposit (zero CJK runs in any variable/value label; the Adolescent .sav is not valid UTF-8 or GB18030 in its header but decoding it yields no CJK strings of length >=2) and the paper and any supplement were unreachable (closed access, 403). Item text, the two instruction sentences and the five anchors are the NCPTSD standard form verbatim (20/20 item strings found in the form text after whitespace collapse); only the item numbers were dropped, and the column header 'In the past month, how much were you bothered by:' was appended to instructions. Which Chinese translation the study used is not known. The past-month reference window is from the IRW dictionary description ('over the past month'), not from the paper. resp: live 0-4, all 20 items; 0 Not at all .. 4 Extremely is the standard PCL-5 scoring and the stored PCL_T equals the plain 0-4 sum (9506/9506). RIGHTS: register verdict ship_with_note applied, not re-derived. NCPTSD page: 'This measure was developed by staff at VA's National Center for PTSD and is in the public domain and not copyrighted.' public_note: Administered in Chinese; the item text shown is the English NCPTSD PCL-5 standard form, and item codes pcl1-pcl20 are assumed to follow its numbering (the deposit confirms each item's DSM-5 cluster but not the order within a cluster).

source_ref: Xiong X, Zhan N, Zou J, Xu F, Geng F (2025) Personality and Individual Differences 246:113343, doi:10.1016/j.paid.2025.113343 (closed access per OpenAlex; not read); data deposit OSF wg568 (view-only link in the IRW dictionary), DERS-16_data/SPSS_data: Adolescent_data.sav (sha256 a89cc7e9f9775586fbca20359796b9c1616032cfcef1f863d7bfb02f189cb7ef), College student_data.sav (99313f8200a04b9b859da37ad23bac78b0095994c661ac3fbb24612cafdc17a2), Community adult_data.sav (651988e66b008ccb5a4eae3244c5f2fe2265edfa026f33e4a30f76d042969f26), Male prisoner_data.sav (c4a88f59c24c34344a66a2df447cb2adfe40e25414f7ce2f36f50848f21383c6), codebook_ders-16.txt; item and option wording from PHQ-9_English.pdf, https://www.phqscreeners.com/images/sites/g/files/g10060481/f/201412/PHQ-9_English.pdf (fetched 2026-09-25, sha256 e3fb5b8853e3530c9025c822b99fd4f4bc17da49eefda5ed689c49238c132a46); instrument Kroenke, Spitzer & Williams (2001) J Gen Intern Med 16(9):606-13; processing script data/ders16_xiong_2025.R
note: MAPPING (paper_order, in the sense of the instrument's printed order): the paper is closed access and the OSF deposit ties phq1..phq9 to no text -- none of the four .sav files carries a variable label or value label on phq1..phq9 (the only labels in the files are the PCL-5 cluster scores R/A/NACM/H, sex, and the *_YN flags), and codebook_ders-16.txt says only 'PHQ = Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9)'. data/ders16_xiong_2025.R melts starts_with('phq') by name, so the IRW code IS the source column name (no positional step); what is inferred is that column phqN is PHQ-9 item N. Tested in verify_phq9_xiong_2025.R (VERDICT: PASS, 9,506 respondents): live per-item x level counts equal the pooled four .sav files in 36/36 cells; phq9 has the lowest mean (0.170) and highest %zero (87.5) of the nine, as the suicidal-ideation item must (next phq8 0.201/84.6); phq3 and the deposit's pcl20 (PCL-5 item 20, trouble falling or staying asleep) are each other's best partner across the 9x20 PHQ x PCL matrix, r 0.595 against runners-up 0.423 (phq4-pcl20) and 0.337 (phq3-pcl11); two-factor blocks hold, within somatic {3,4,5} 0.512 and within cognitive {2,6,7,8,9} 0.431 vs 0.412 across (the cognitive margin is thin). Not established: phq4 vs phq5, the order among phq2/phq6/phq7/phq8, and phq1 -- hence PARTIAL. Not used as evidence: phq7's best PCL partner is pcl19 (concentration, 0.383) but pcl19's best PHQ partner is phq6 (0.385), so that twin is not mutual. OPTIONS: the PHQ-9 form prints 0/1/2/3 beside Not at all / Several days / More than half the days / Nearly every day. Deposit corroborates raw 0-3 storage in that direction: PHQ_T equals the row sum of phq1..9 exactly (max abs diff 0), and PHQ_YN equals (PHQ_T >= 10), the PHQ-9's standard cut-off, for all 9,506 rows (8651/855, zero disagreements); phq9 at 87.5% zero is only coherent with 0 = Not at all. TEXT: transcribed verbatim from PHQ-9_English.pdf, including the em dashes in items 6 and 8 and item 8's internal question mark; leading numbers stripped and line wraps joined with single spaces. Instructions ship the form's question sentence only; the paper-form parenthetical '(Use “✔” to indicate your answer)' and the unnumbered tenth functional-difficulty question (not in the live data) were not shipped. LANGUAGE: the four samples are Chinese (dictionary description: 'four Chinese samples'); no Chinese wording exists in the deposit (all four .sav files read, zero CJK characters in any variable or value label; codebook is English) and the paper was not accessible, so the fallback applies: English in the base fields, no _translated columns, language=Chinese. Which Chinese PHQ-9 translation was administered is not recorded in anything read. RIGHTS: instrument_rights_register row 'PHQ and GAD screener family' = ship (express grant), applied; the fetched PDF's footer reads 'No permission required to reproduce, translate, display or distribute.' STEP 3b: clean -- 9 items, resp 0-3, PHQ_T range 0-27 match the PHQ-9 and not the LEC-5 (17 items), PCL-5 (20 items, 0-4) or DERS-16 in the same files. DATA NOTE (not a defect): the processing script reads Adolescent_data.csv while the OSF deposit now holds Adolescent_data.sav; the live table still matches the .sav cell for cell. The pooled table mixes adolescents (5,927), college students (1,466), community adults (701) and male prisoners (1,412) with no sample covariate, and Adolescent_data.sav only parses as latin1 (non-UTF-8 bytes) though it contains no Chinese text. SIBLINGS lec5_xiong_2025 and pcl5_xiong_2025 (same deposit) are owned by other agents; nothing was written for them. xiong_2025_dass21 is a different study (different processing script data/xiong_2025_dass21.py) and was not consulted.
public_note: The PHQ-9 was administered in Chinese, but no Chinese wording is published in this study's data deposit and its paper is not open access, so the item and option text shipped here is the instrument publisher's official English (phqscreeners.com) rather than the sentences respondents read.
